title: Misery
author: King, Stephen
review:
Absolutely loved it, definitely one of my favorite King books now. I really enjoy the lack of supernatural elements as well.

What King can do with two characters in a single location is mind blowing, it stays interesting, exciting, and horrific until the end. Annie Wilkes is a great character and antagonist. Lots of disturbing stuff here to chew on.

The commentary and themes of an author's relationship with his fans, his work, and himself lands really well and you can tell it is almost autobiographical as some of the best stories are. A really unique horror story that I'll be thinking about for a long time, should have read this sooner.

But his ideas about God—like his ideas about so many things, had changed. They had changed in Africa. In Africa he had discovered that there was not just one God but many, and some were more than cruel—they were insane, and that changed all. Cruelty, after all, was understandable. With insanity, however, there was no arguing.
Writing may be masturbatory, but God forbid it should be an act of autocannibalism.
